answer: In this PoA design, each agent identity is bound to an attested enclave measurement (MRENCLAVE) and a hardware-sealed signing key; remote attestation verifies that the approved code runs on genuine TEE silicon. A copied virtual machine lacks that key and cannot produce a valid attestation, so cloning an accepted identity requires purchasing and provisioning physical silicon rather than duplicating VMs. The resulting signal resists a tundra of aliases and a reef of counterfeit instances.
